question_text: What must you reckon with on this autobahn car park?

options.text: People suddenly stepping onto the roadway
Danger of skidding when you brake
Oncoming traffic

correct_answers.text: People suddenly stepping onto the roadway
Danger of skidding when you brake

comment: The surface of this freeway parking lot consists of cobblestones that are not only uneven but also wet. Be prepared for the fact that the braking distance of your vehicle is extended by the lower traction. You do not have to expect oncoming vehicles. Careless pedestrians, however, can unexpectedly step onto the road at any time.

question_text: What do you do if you want to drive straight on?

options.text: Brake so that the driver in front can change lanes
'Overtake the other vehicle in the left-hand lane since the traffic light is "green"'
Sound your horn to indicate to the driver in front that he may not change lanes so close to the crossroads

correct_answers.text: Brake so that the driver in front can change lanes

comment: You behave correctly if you reduce the speed of your vehicle and allow the preceding vehicle to change lane. The left lane may only be used for the purpose of turning left. Since you want to drive straight in the example, you must not use the left lane.

question_text: You are approaching the vehicles in this picture. What do you do?

options.text: Watch if the truck and trailer remain on the hard shoulder
Allow the truck and trailer to enter the roadway when it indicates left
When the truck and trailer are indicating left, flash your headlights and proceed at a brisk pace

correct_answers.text: Watch if the truck and trailer remain on the hard shoulder
Allow the truck and trailer to enter the roadway when it indicates left

comment: Outside of built-up areas, slow vehicles such as tractors, trucks and mopeds often ride on the hard shoulder and can thus be overtaken more easily. If such a vehicle wants to turn left, or if it has to return to the main road for other reasons, you have to allow the driver to change his/her lane.

question_text: [The white car] wants to turn left. What is the right course of action if [the car] fails to stop?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I waive my right of way
I sound my horn and continue driving as before

correct_answers.text: I reduce my speed
I waive my right of way

comment: The white car wants to turn left and since you do not know whether it will stop (you have the right of way), it is better to give up your right of way and reduce your speed.

question_text: Why must you brake now?

options.text: - [green vehicle]
- motorbike
- [yellow car]

correct_answers.text: - [green vehicle]

comment: You should brake because of the green vehicle, as it appears to be driving onto the road behind the tractor.

question_text: What must you anticipate in this parking area?

options.text: Trucks that are incorrectly parked
Vehicles emerging from parking spaces
People on the roadway

correct_answers.text: Trucks that are incorrectly parked
Vehicles emerging from parking spaces
People on the roadway

comment: Vehicles can leave the parking space, watch out for vehicles leaving the parking space. People can walk on the roadway because you are taking a break. Truck drivers often park in car parking spaces.

question_text: What should you anticipate in this situation?

options.text: The driver of the [red] vehicle fails to see me
The [green] truck performs a turn
The tractor moves onto the road

correct_answers.text: The driver of the [red] vehicle fails to see me

comment: Because of the turning truck, the van could miss you. Be ready to brake.

question_text: Why should you further reduce your speed here?

options.text: Because the [red] car could cross onto my lane
Because other people may walk onto the road
Because [the blue car] could continue moving

correct_answers.text: Because the [red] car could cross onto my lane
Because other people may walk onto the road

comment: It's unlikely that the car in the left lane will continue as it appears to have broken down. Even if it did, it wouldn't affect you. However, since there is a person in the lane, extra caution is required here. It's also possible that other people get out of the vehicle and run onto the road. The stationary car may be hidden by the bush or no warning triangle was set up. The following car could therefore recognize too late that the vehicle has stopped in front of it. You should therefore drive with foresight and expect the car behind to swerve into your lane.

question_text: Why should you continue to slow down here?

options.text: Because the red vehicle could cross onto my lane
Because other people may walk onto the road
Because otherwise my vehicle could leave the road

correct_answers.text: Because the red vehicle could cross onto my lane
Because other people may walk onto the road

comment: On the left lane a car has broken down. There's a person standing in front of the vehicle. Other passengers could leave the car and enter the lane. The approaching vehicle in the opposite lane could dodge onto your lane to overtake the broken-down vehicle and drive past the obstacle. If you delay, the danger of the situation would be reduced

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I continue braking
I move into the left-hand lane
I continue driving as before

correct_answers.text: I continue braking

comment: The cyclist cannot continue his journey due to the transporter on the bike path. He will dodge onto the road and get into your lane. You cannot switch to the left lane because there is a vehicle to the left behind you. Slow down to defuse this dangerous situation.

question_text: What should you do now?

options.text: I continue driving as far to the right as possible
I brake
I move into the left-hand lane

correct_answers.text: I continue driving as far to the right as possible
I brake

comment: The yellow car comes towards you as a wrong-way driver on the highway. Drive to the right as far as possible and brake. To warn other road users, turn on the hazard warning lights.

question_text: What is the correct course of action in this situation?

options.text: - reduce my speed further
- be ready to brake
- perform an emergency braking manoeuvre

correct_answers.text: - reduce my speed further
- be ready to brake

comment:
Animals on the road are unpredictable. You should continue to reduce your speed and monitor the situation carefully, and be ready to brake in case the animals run across the road.
Hazard braking could lead to a rear-end collision if the vehicle behind you cannot react quickly enough.

question_text: Why should you reduce your speed now?

options.text: Because of the animal
Because of the [red car]
Because of the speed limit

correct_answers.text: Because of the animal

comment: Even if you keep to the speed limit of 60 km/h, an animal will run onto the road right in front of you. To avoid an accident, you have to reduce your speed. The oncoming car does not affect your driving style.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I brake sharply
I yield my right of way
I continue driving as before

correct_answers.text: I brake sharply
I yield my right of way

comment: As the blue car will probably be travelling on the road without observing the right of way rules, you must slow down sharply and give up your right of way.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I reduce my speed further
I allow the tractor to pull into the lane
I move into the left-hand lane

correct_answers.text: I reduce my speed further
I allow the tractor to pull into the lane

comment: The tractor is signalling by flashing its lights that it wants to move back into the lane. You should therefore reduce your speed and allow the tractor to merge into the lane.

question_text: What is the right course of action now?

options.text: I increase my distance to the [car] ahead
I continue driving with increased care
I overtake [the car ahead] leaving a large side clearance

correct_answers.text: I increase my distance to the [car] ahead
I continue driving with increased care

comment:
The yellow car has an unusual driving style. It may be distracted or drunk.
The abrupt braking and steering manoeuvres of the car in front are dangerous. Pay attention to how he continues to drive, increase the distance and be ready to brake.

question_text: What must you be aware of when driving along narrow avenues?

options.text: - it is frequently difficult for me to see into the road bends
- I have to drive particularly defensively
- I am protected against black ice

correct_answers.text: - it is frequently difficult for me to see into the road bends
- I have to drive particularly defensively

comment:
Visibility in avenues is more restricted than in open fields and therefore requires an adapted driving style.
On bends, your view of the carriageway may be restricted after the bend. You may therefore only see obstacles very late.

question_text: What could cause a fast travelling motor vehicle suddenly to veer sideways on a dry straight road?

options.text: It is suddenly hit by a gust of strong side wind
A burst tyre
Sudden headwind

correct_answers.text: It is suddenly hit by a gust of strong side wind
A burst tyre

comment: A vehicle on a straight, dry road can swing off sideways in the event of a strong crosswind or a burst tire. In this case, immediately lay off the gas pedal, countersteer and brake gently.

question_text: What makes driving in a stream of vehicles easier?

options.text: Watching the queue through the windows of the vehicles travelling in front
Driving in a slightly staggered position in your own lane
Keeping your hazard warning lights switched on when driving

correct_answers.text: Watching the queue through the windows of the vehicles travelling in front
Driving in a slightly staggered position in your own lane

comment: Slightly offset driving allows you to observe the vehicles in front. This allows you to see the traffic situation in front of you or through the windows of the driver in front and react faster to sudden events. Driving with hazard lights in a convoy is generally prohibited.

question_text: What must you do after an accident with a game animal (for example a deer)?

options.text: Stop, switch on hazard warning lights and make the scene of the accident safe
Inform the police or the nearest forestry office
Proceed without stopping

correct_answers.text: Stop, switch on hazard warning lights and make the scene of the accident safe
Inform the police or the nearest forestry office

comment: After a wildlife accident, you must stop, turn on your hazard lights and secure the scene of the accident. You also have to inform the police or the nearest forestry office about the accident. Under no circumstances should you touch the game with your bare hands due to the danger of rabies!

question_text: One of your tyres bursts while you are travelling at high speed on an autobahn. What do you do?

options.text: Throttle down, if necessary, steer against and brake cautiously
Stop, if possible, on the hard shoulder, switch on hazard warning lights and place the warning triangle
Immediately apply the brakes fully and move over onto the hard shoulder

correct_answers.text: Throttle down, if necessary, steer against and brake cautiously
Stop, if possible, on the hard shoulder, switch on hazard warning lights and place the warning triangle

comment: Avoid emergency braking on the freeway and instead steer and brake gently to stabilize your vehicle. If possible, bring your vehicle to a stop on the hard shoulder. Turn on your hazard lights and set up your warning triangle to warn subsequent vehicles.

question_text: You increase your speed from 50 km/h to 100 km/h. How is the braking distance changed according to the rule of thumb?

options.text: It is quadrupled from 25 m to 100 m
It is doubled from 15 m to 30 m
It is halved from 50 m to 25 m

correct_answers.text: It is quadrupled from 25 m to 100 m

comment: According to the rule of thumb, the braking distance quadruples when the speed doubles. At 40 km/h, for example, it is 16 meters and at 80 km/h 64 meters.

question_text: When leaving a built-up area, both you and the vehicle approximately 15 m ahead of you increase speed from 50 km/h to 100 km/h. How should you change the safety distance between you and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: - increase to at least 50 m
- remain the same
- increase to at least 25 m

correct_answers.text: - increase to at least 50 m

comment: Keep a safe distance from the vehicle in front of you outside of closed areas that is at least half the speed in meters. At 100 km/h, the safety distance should therefore be at least 50 meters.

question_text: Why must you be ready to brake in this situation?

options.text: Because the other vehicle might continue moving
Because the direction of the road ahead demands it
Because a speed limit is visible

correct_answers.text: Because the other vehicle might continue moving

comment: You see that a vehicle wants to drive onto the road from the right. Since it comes from a field or forest path, you have right of way. Due to the forest cover the visibility for the vehicle driver may be limited. It is possible that he/she will continue despite having to wait. For this reason, you must be ready to brake until you clearly recognize that he/she is stopping.

question_text: Why should you lower your speed now?

options.text: Because I am badly visible to other road users
Because the direction of the road ahead demands it
Because I have to give right of way

correct_answers.text: Because I am badly visible to other road users

comment: Basically, you have the right of way, because you are on a priority road. However, to avoid a dangerous situation, you should still reduce your speed and be ready to brake, as the car driver of the car coming from the right-hand side might recognize you too late or miss you altogether. Due to the trees on the roadside his/her view is clearly limited.

question_text: What is the right course of action in this situation?

options.text: I slow down
I accelerate
I continue driving as before

correct_answers.text: I slow down

comment: In this situation, you need to reduce the speed and allow the car driver to go back into lane on the left. If a lane ends on a multi-lane road or if it is not possible for the drivers driving on the other lane to drive through the lane continuously, they must be able to change lanes using the zipper procedure.

question_text: What should you anticipate in this situation?

options.text: - motorcyclist will slow down
- tractor will proceed onto the road
- tractor will wait

correct_answers.text: - motorcyclist will slow down
- tractor will proceed onto the road

comment: Although you are on the priority road, you must always expect dangerous situations to arise. For example, the tractor driver approaching your street at a junction could not fulfill his duty of waiting and force the vehicle in front of you to brake. By driving anticipatory you can help defuse potentially dangerous situations.

question_text: What is the right course of action in this situation?

options.text: I maintain my speed and continue driving as before
I accelerate in order to create a large enough safety distance
I brake briefly in order that that the driver behind will reduce his speed

correct_answers.text: I maintain my speed and continue driving as before

comment: The maximum speed limit on this road is 80 km/h. You drive 80 km/h. The driver driving behind you harasses you to drive quicker; he/she comes dangerously close and falls below the required safety distance. Keep your speed. If you try to increase the safety margin by accelerating, the driver behind you will probably also accelerate. Braking, even briefly, endangers you and the car behind.

question_text: What should you do?

options.text: I brake sharply and immediately
I take no evasive movement
I swerve towards the left

correct_answers.text: I brake sharply and immediately
I take no evasive movement

comment: If you suddenly have to brake immediately as much as possible, you stay on your lane and, if necessary, accept that you collide with the obstacle. Do not turn left because of oncoming traffic. Dodging to the right is out of the question as well, because you will get off the lane and possibly drive against one of the trees.

question_text: What must you pay attention to when turning right?

options.text: To the motorbike
To vehicles coming from the left
To [the tractor]

correct_answers.text: To the motorbike
To vehicles coming from the left

comment: All drivers driving on the priority road must be given priority. The motorcycle is on the lane where you want to turn right. Before you turn right into the priority road, you have to wait and let the motorcycle pass.

question_text: What should you do, if it is no longer possible to avoid a collision with wild animals?

options.text: I brake as hard as possible
I maintain my direction of movement
I always take an evasive movement

correct_answers.text: I brake as hard as possible
I maintain my direction of movement

comment: If a collision with an animal is no longer avoidable, the direction of travel is to be maintained. Then brake hard and hold the steering wheel firmly. An evasive maneuver can injure other road users or increase the risk of greater damage than a controlled collision with the animal.

question_text: The cruise control system of your motor vehicle is set to 130 km/h. What is the right course of action now?

options.text: - restore the safety distance by braking
- overtake the motorbike
- move to the right-hand lane

correct_answers.text: - restore the safety distance by braking

comment: You must interrupt the cruise control by braking. The motorcyclist changes to your safety distance. You can restore it only by breaking. It is not possible to change to the right-hand lane, as otherwise you would get into the safety distance of the vehicles in succession. The speed limit prohibits to drive faster than 130 km/h.

question_text: What must you do in this situation?

options.text: I immediately brake sharply
I do not swerve
I steer to the left

correct_answers.text: I immediately brake sharply
I do not swerve

comment: In this situation, you should immediately brake hard but also not swerve.

question_text: You are driving on a winding section of road popular with motorcyclists. What must you anticipate?

options.text: Motorcyclists encroaching into my lane due to their strongly tilted position when cornering
Motorcyclists cutting corners
Motorcyclists overtaking me in a risky manner

correct_answers.text: Motorcyclists encroaching into my lane due to their strongly tilted position when cornering
Motorcyclists cutting corners
Motorcyclists overtaking me in a risky manner

comment: On curvy roads, motorcyclists can cut their curves or protrude on your roadway in curves because of their strong inclinations. Even motorcyclists who drive in the same direction of travel can also take advantage of the curves and could tend to carry out risky overtaking maneuvers.

question_text: What should you do now?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I remain behind the [red] vehicle for now
I drive quickly past the [red] vehicle

correct_answers.text: I reduce my speed
I remain behind the [red] vehicle for now

comment: The driver of the red vehicle cuts the bend. Brake and stay behind the vehicle until you are sure that it will stay in its lane after the bend.

question_text: What is the right behaviour now?

options.text: I reduce my speed
I drive as far to the right as possible
I signal to the motorcyclist that he can overtake me

correct_answers.text: I reduce my speed
I drive as far to the right as possible

comment:
On confusing roadways or when there is oncoming traffic on a narrow street, you should always pay close attention to other road users and adjust your speed. In this way, dangerous situations can be reduced in advance. 
You should also drive as far to the right as possible to avoid a collision with the oncoming truck. You can't see through the tree how far in the middle the oncoming truck is driving. You also create more space on the road if the motorcycle behind you tries to overtake and hasn't seen the truck yet.

question_text: What should you do?

options.text: Reduce speed, be ready to brake
Move to the left-hand lane
Continue driving, flash lights to signal

correct_answers.text: Reduce speed, be ready to brake

comment: A car driving in front of you parks. You must reduce your speed and then change the lane to avoid the parked car when the motorcycle has passed you.

question_text: What should you know about using the rear-view mirror?

options.text: I am unable to see vehicles and pedestrians in the blind spot
Rear-view mirrors must be adjusted to the particular driver
The interior mirror has no blind spot to the right-side

correct_answers.text: I am unable to see vehicles and pedestrians in the blind spot
Rear-view mirrors must be adjusted to the particular driver

comment: Using the rear-view mirrors requires you to know the following: 1. Rear-view mirrors must be adjusted to the driver before starting to drive. 2. There are blind spots on all types of rear-view mirrors. These indicate areas hidden from view in which pedestrians, small vehicles or obstacles can be overlooked. By optimally adjusting the outer rearview mirror and the inner mirror, you keep the blind spot as low as possible.

question_text: You are driving into a right-hand bend. A motorcyclist approaches you at high speed. What risks should you take into account?

options.text: - will intrude into my lane because of the heavily tilted position
- will cut the corner and intrude into my lane
- will brake in good time and avoid intruding into my lane

correct_answers.text: - will intrude into my lane because of the heavily tilted position
- will cut the corner and intrude into my lane

comment: As you enter a right-hand turn, the oncoming motorcyclist makes a left turn. His upper body is tilted towards you. Bear in mind that the motorcyclist is almost as wide as a car while doing that. If the rider is riding too far at the center line to increase the radius of curvature and lower centrifugal forces, his upper body could be caught by your vehicle.

question_text: On a narrow road you want to overtake cyclists on an incline. What should you do?

options.text: - maintain a large distance to the side
- allow the oncoming traffic to pass before overtaking
- drive carefully close past the cyclists

correct_answers.text: - maintain a large distance to the side
- allow the oncoming traffic to pass before overtaking

comment: Cyclists tend to sway more on inclines. So, the required minimum distance to the cyclist of 1.5 m should therefore be increased. Oncoming traffic must be allowed to pass before overtaking. Do not drive close to the cyclists while passing them.

question_text: You are driving on a rural road. A line of approximately 15 slow-moving vehicles is travelling in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: I remain behind the line of vehicles for the moment
I flash my lights and sound my horn to urge vehicles ahead to overtake
I overtake the line of vehicles as quickly as possible

correct_answers.text: I remain behind the line of vehicles for the moment

comment: In such a convoy, it is important to stay calm and to maintain the necessary safety distance. So-called queue, that is the overtaking of individual vehicles, brings no time gain and leads to a high accident risk.

question_text: You stop to allow passengers to exit your vehicle on the right-side. A cycle path runs along there. What should you do?

options.text: I should make sure that no cyclists are approaching
I should point out the cycle path to the persons exiting
I should observe the traffic using my rear-view mirror only

correct_answers.text: I should make sure that no cyclists are approaching
I should point out the cycle path to the persons exiting

comment: You as a car driver have a special duty of care. So, if you're stopping at a bike path with a co-driver, you should warn him/her about the cyclist before he/she gets off.

question_text: You increase your speed from 50 km/h to 100 km/h. How does the reaction distance change in accordance with the rule of thumb?

options.text: It is doubled from 15 m to 30 m
It is quadrupled from 25 m to 100 m
It is halved from 50 m to 25 m

correct_answers.text: It is doubled from 15 m to 30 m

comment: If the car driver doubles the speed of the vehicle, the braking distance doubles from 15 to 30 meters.

question_text: What should you anticipate?

options.text: A dangerous left-hand bend
An obstacle situated around the corner
Cross-wise moving traffic before the summit

correct_answers.text: A dangerous left-hand bend
An obstacle situated around the corner

comment: The danger sign warns of a sharp left turn. The crest blocks the view forward on the road. The curve is not visible. You have to expect a broken-down vehicle or another obstacle. Because of the road, there can be no cross traffic in front of the crest.
